frontier: Minimum total native unit-step cost of an unrestricted transversal repair equals an assignment in the finite Cayley quotient.
An optimal total-cost solution can keep one original point in every occupied coset and move exactly the collision deficit many points.
The same minimum total cost admits a no-physical-collision relay of native unit moves, at the price of extra internal steps and possibly moving more labels.
A bounded maximum displacement is characterized by the weighted-fiber Hall condition; minimal moved count and minimal maximum displacement can conflict.

For the old and conjugate chains at p congruent to 3 mod 4, minimum repair cost divided by p squared tends to 1/4. Ignoring any fixed subset of native coordinates yields a separate volume lower bound.
Adaptive compact cyclic kernels can have much lower costs but remain different lattices and retain their cross-base divisibility obstruction. Box-constrained repair needs a different cost observer.
